candidates.computation_change_reason: Identifies the parameter category for a discharge-limit obligation; different readings of what falls under floating solids or visible foam would change which measurements are paired with this limit in Purpose A.

candidates.exact_span: There shall be no discharge of oils, scum, grease and other floating materials that would cause the formation of a visible sheen or visible deposits on the bottom or shoreline, or would damage or impair the normal growth, function or reproduction of human, animal, plant or aquatic life.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets a qualitative, non-numeric discharge standard with effect-based triggers ('would cause', 'would damage or impair'); interpretation of whether this is an enforceable numeric limit, how to compare reported measurements to it, and how to classify periods without ordinary numeric results would change Purpose A limit-applicability logic and Purpose C missing-evidence semantics.

candidates.exact_span: B.     REPORTING OF MONITORING RESULTS (MINOR DISCHARGERS)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Scopes the following monitoring and reporting obligations to minor dischargers; whether a facility falls within that class changes which monitoring requirements are applicable under Purpose B.

candidates.exact_span: Discharge Monitoring Report (DMR) results shall be electronically reported to EPA per 40 CFR 127.16.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes that DMR monitoring results are a required reporting obligation; interpretation of what counts as a DMR result and when electronic submission is required affects which monitoring requirements are treated as applicable in Purpose B.

candidates.exact_span: Monitoring information shall be submitted quarterly.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Imposes a quarterly monitoring-information submission obligation; different readings of what 'monitoring information' encompasses or whether quarterly submission was required for a given period would change Purpose B applicability and Purpose C classification of missing or non-numeric evidence.

candidates.exact_span: Each quarterly submittal shall include separate forms for each month of the reporting period.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Requires monthly monitoring forms within each quarterly reporting cycle; interpretation of this monthly granularity affects which monitoring periods are obligated in Purpose B and whether absent monthly forms constitute missing required evidence in Purpose C.

candidates.exact_span: Reporting periods shall end on the last day of the months March, June, September, and December.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines the calendar boundaries of reporting periods; for Federal FY2025, different interpretations of how these quarter-end dates map to obligated monitoring periods would change which requirements are evaluated in Purpose B and which no-result intervals are assessed in Purpose C.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee is required to submit regular quarterly reports as described above postmarked no later than the 28th day of the month following each reporting period.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets a deadline for quarterly report submission; interpretation of when a reporting period's evidence is due versus merely required affects Purpose B monitoring-obligation timing and Purpose C judgments about whether adequate monitoring evidence should exist for a given period.
